text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today as oil markets stabilized following three days of declines. The main driver was news that Saudi Arabia is releasing additional crude supplies to offset disruptions, which eased fears of a prolonged supply crunch. U.S. crude prices have fallen sharply—dipping below $100 per barrel on Friday—but the stock held up reasonably well, suggesting investors see the stabilization as positive for the company's medium-term outlook.

The broader context here is geopolitical: an ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and Houthi attacks have threatened Middle Eastern oil supplies, but signals of a potential diplomatic resolution (Trump indicated the U.S. may be nearing an end to the conflict) combined with Saudi output increases have reduced immediate supply panic. With crude still trading above $130 globally, the worst-case scenario for oil producers appears to have been avoided—at least for now.
